Alice (PM): quick sync — we need to decide scope + launch criteria for the tool/function-calling API change. two competing asks: strict tool schemas (enterprise customers) vs flexible looser runtime (self-serve devs). what should we prioritize for Q2?
Ben (API): can we bullet the real customer asks? i've seen 3 asks: 1) deterministic schema validation and error codes, 2) streaming tool outputs with partial result updates, 3) versioned tool contracts.
Emily (CS): +1 on deterministic validation — a fintech pilot said they can only accept responses that strictly match a JSON schema. they'd need a signed migration path.
Charlie (Eng): technically strict schema checks add latency and complexity. we can validate at the node/proxy layer rather than the hot inference path, but that impacts error surface for streaming.
Devon (Product): launch criteria proposal: must support 1) schema registration + versioning, 2) runtime validation with clear error codes, 3) docs + SDK helpers for glue. stretch: streaming tool outputs.
Ben (API): proposal for API surface: incoming tool spec: {"name":"str","inputs": {"type":"json-schema","schema_id":"v1"}, "idempotency":"optional"}. call message: {"tool":"name","args_ref":"blob|inline"}. result message: {"tool":"name","status":"ok|error","payload_ref":"blob","schema_id":"v1"}. keep it simple.
Charlie (Eng): pseudo-code note: for streaming we need a chunk envelope: ```event: chunk, seq: 1, body: {...}, partial: true``` plus finalization event. that also needs to carry schema checkpoints so consumers can validate incrementally.
Emily (CS): customers will expect clear mapping: if schema validation fails, what happens to the call? immediate 400-like error back to app or allow tool to run and flag result as invalid? fintech wants reject-before-run.
Alice (PM): decision points we need to capture: A) pre-exec strict validation vs post-exec flagging, B) streaming support on day one or v2, C) server-side schema registry vs user-managed. recommendation: do A conservative (reject-before-run for enterprise tier), B = v2 (opt-in alpha), C = server-side registry + webhooks for changes.
Ben (API): agree on A conservative — implement a validation-mode flag per customer/route (enforced by control plane). that enables Dedicated/Private to opt-in without impacting hosted self-serve.
Charlie (Eng): implementation notes: control-plane flag + validation workers that run async preflight. if validation fails we short-circuit with a standardized error payload: {"code":"tool.schema_mismatch","details":"..."}. low runtime overhead for hot path.
Devon (Product): launch checklist draft: 1) API spec v1 doc, 2) SDK helpers (python/js) with schema bundling, 3) schema registry UI + ACLs, 4) canary with 2 customers (finance + marketplace), 5) observability: per-call validation metrics.
Emily (CS): I'll line up the fintech pilot for canary and prepare migration docs. also ask legal about schema retention policies.
Ben (API): TODOs: i'll draft the OpenAPI-like spec and example JSON schema payloads. Charlie — can you estimate engineering effort for validation workers + registry?
Charlie (Eng): roughs: validation workers + infra ~3 weeks, registry UI + ACLs ~2 weeks, streaming envelope work (v2) ~4 weeks. depends on priority and overlapping work.
Alice (PM): OK let's prioritize: 1) validation workers + control-plane flag (P0), 2) API spec + SDKs (P0), 3) registry backend (P1), 4) registry UI (P2), 5) streaming (P3). timeline: aim for alpha in 6 weeks for enterprise customers.
OpsBot (bot): Created ticket PROD-3421 "tool-call: validation-mode + schema workers" assigned to @Charlie (Eng).
Devon (Product): risk note: backward compatibility — we must support unversioned tools for legacy customers and provide migration tools (lint/bundle).
Ben (API): one more: telemetry events need to include schema_id and validation result for signal. add to roadmap.
Alice (PM): great. Emily please confirm pilot readiness by next Tue. Charlie + Ben sync to draft spec by EOD Fri. will follow-up with a short PRD. :thumbsup:
